name: Esteros del Iberá
tagline: A vast, quiet wetland of floating islands and lagoons, alive with caimans, capybaras and birds, where jaguars are being brought back to the wild.
highlight: Drifting in a small boat at dawn among floating islands, with caimans, capybaras and hundreds of birds in every direction.
shortDescription: One of South America's largest freshwater wetlands, a remote nature reserve of lagoons and marshes, with boat safaris, walking, horse riding, and a pioneering rewilding project.
metaDescription: An Esteros del Iberá travel guide: boat safaris, caimans, capybaras, birdlife, Colonia Carlos Pellegrini, the jaguar rewilding project, best time, how to get there and a three-day plan.
nearestAirport: Corrientes (CNQ) or Posadas (PSS), about 4 to 5 hours' drive
knownFor: Wetland wildlife, caimans, capybaras, birds, rewilding, quiet
budget: US$120–300 per day, mid-range, with lodge stays

image.alt: A calm lagoon covered with aquatic plants in the Esteros del Iberá wetlands

intro: The Esteros del Iberá is one of the largest freshwater wetlands in South America, an area of about 13,000 square kilometres of lagoons, marshes and floating islands, fed by rainfall rather than rivers, in the province of Corrientes. Its shallow, still waters are covered with aquatic plants, and much of the surface is made up of camalotes, floating mats of vegetation. It is home to more than 350 species of bird, and to caimans, capybaras, marsh deer, howler monkeys and many others.

For decades, poaching and cattle ranching reduced the wildlife, but a large conservation project, begun by the American philanthropist Douglas Tompkins and continued by his foundation and the Argentine government, has bought and donated land, creating Iberá National Park in 2018. The project has reintroduced species that had disappeared from the area, including giant anteaters, pampas deer, giant otters and, in recent years, jaguars, and it is one of the most ambitious rewilding projects in South America.

Iberá is remote and quiet. The main base is the small village of Colonia Carlos Pellegrini, on the edge of a large lagoon, where lodges and guesthouses offer boat trips, walks, horseback rides and night safaris. It is not an easy place to reach, and it is not for those who want a big-name attraction, but it is a peaceful and rewarding place for wildlife lovers.

whyVisit.intro: Iberá offers close encounters with wetland wildlife in a quiet, uncrowded setting, and a chance to support conservation.

points.title: Wildlife everywhere
points.text: Caimans, capybaras, marsh deer, howler monkeys and hundreds of bird species.

points.title: Quiet boat safaris
points.text: Small motorless or low-noise boats drift through lagoons and among floating islands.

points.title: Rewilding in action
points.text: A project bringing back anteaters, otters, deer and even jaguars.

points.title: Peace and stars
points.text: Dark skies and a slow pace.

attractionsIntro: Most experiences are guided, from Colonia Carlos Pellegrini and nearby lodges.

attractions.name: Laguna Iberá boat safari

image.alt: A marsh of floating vegetation and water plants in the Iberá wetlands

attractions.text: A boat trip on the large lagoon beside Carlos Pellegrini, with a guide who spots caimans, capybaras, snail kites and marsh deer among the floating islands.
attractions.tip: Go at dawn or late afternoon.

attractions.name: Caimans and capybaras

image.alt: A yacaré caiman resting on the bank in the Iberá wetlands

attractions.text: Yacaré caimans bask on banks and capybaras graze in groups, often at close range, in a landscape where wildlife has little fear of people.

attractions.name: Birdwatching

image.alt: A saffron finch perched among reeds in the Iberá wetlands

attractions.text: More than 350 species, including jabiru storks, herons, spoonbills, ducks, kingfishers and the rare strange-tailed tyrant.

attractions.name: The Laguna Iberá lookout
attractions.text: A viewpoint over the lagoon, near the village, for sunset.

attractions.name: Rewilding centres
attractions.text: Visitors can see where jaguars, giant otters and other species are prepared for release, though not the animals themselves in some cases.
attractions.tip: Ask a guide about the project.

attractions.name: Flying over the marshes

image.file: File:Flying Over Esteros del Iberá The kingdom of water, North-eastern Argentina.jpg
image.alt: An aerial view of the Iberá wetlands with lagoons and floating vegetation

attractions.text: The vast scale of the wetland is best seen from above, on a small-plane flight.

thingsToDoIntro: Activities are quiet, guided and wildlife-focused.

thingsToDo.title: Take a boat safari
thingsToDo.text: Drift among floating islands, spotting wildlife.

thingsToDo.title: Go on a night safari
thingsToDo.text: See caimans, owls and nocturnal mammals by torchlight.

thingsToDo.title: Ride a horse
thingsToDo.text: Gaucho-led rides through the marsh edge.

thingsToDo.title: Walk with a guide
thingsToDo.text: Trails through palm savannah and wetland edges.

foodIntro: Food in Iberá is simple and regional, with river fish, beef and local sweets.

foods.name: Surubí and pacú
foods.text: River fish, grilled or in stews.

foods.name: Mbaipy and sopa paraguaya
foods.text: Corn-based dishes of the Guaraní tradition.

areas.text: Lodges and guesthouses beside the lagoon.

areas.text: Small lodges at other sides of the wetland.

gettingThere.intro: Iberá is remote, and reached by road, with some unpaved sections.

options.mode: Fly to Corrientes or Posadas, then drive
options.text: About 4 to 5 hours from either airport, with the last stretch unpaved.
options.detail: Hire a car or arrange a transfer.

options.text: Lodges arrange transfers from airports and Iguazú.
Buses reach Mercedes, about 120 km from Carlos Pellegrini.

gettingAround.intro: Everything is guided and close to Carlos Pellegrini.

options.text: The main way to see wildlife.

bestTime.headline: March–November
bestTime.summary: Iberá has a humid subtropical climate, with hot, rainy summers and mild winters. Winter is cooler and drier, with fewer insects.

seasons.text: Hot, humid and rainy, with mosquitoes.
Mild days, cool nights and fewer insects.
Warm, with birds in breeding plumage.

bestTime.avoid: January and February for heat and insects.

itinerary.title: Three days in Iberá
itinerary.intro: Boats, walks and a night safari.

days.title: Arrive
days.afternoon: A walk and a lagoon lookout.

tipsIntro: A few tips make the visit more comfortable.
tips: Visit between March and November, avoiding the summer heat and insects.
Bring insect repellent, sun protection, binoculars and a hat.
Book lodges and transfers in advance.
Carry cash, since there are few ATMs.
Do not feed animals, and keep a safe distance.
Take a night safari for different wildlife.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Iberá?

faq.a: The rewilding project has released jaguars, but sightings are rare. Caimans, capybaras and birds are much easier.

faq.q: What is the best time to visit?

faq.a: By road from Corrientes or Posadas, about 4 to 5 hours, or by lodge transfer.
